Management Plan

- Assessed as localized allergic reaction following wasp/bee sting; no evidence of systemic or anaphylactic reaction at assessment
- Advised to purchase and take over-the-counter antihistamines (e.g., Piriton/chlorphenamine 4 mg up to six times/day or a once-daily antihistamine)
- Provided education about signs of anaphylaxis, including symptoms to monitor (swelling of lips, breathing difficulty, stridor)
- Advised urgent evaluation if symptoms worsen (especially breathing or swelling); to seek emergency care if rapid progression
- Education link for information about anaphylactic reactions to be provided
- Advised to watch for signs of infection at sting site (increasing redness, heat)
- Informed that allergy testing is not indicated unless reactions become recurrent
- No investigations or referrals arranged at this time
- No follow-up appointment booked; advised to reconsult if further concerns arise
